markets: Sells in South Korea and export markets in Europe, the Middle East and elsewhere; taken over by KG Group.
rationale: Mid-size Korean automaker seeking export growth and brand renewal; F1 could aid awareness, though finances are modest.
changed: Renamed from SsangYong Motor in 2023 after KG Group takeover

name: Autonomous Solutions
desc: Develops autonomous vehicle control software and retrofit kits for industrial fleets such as mining haul trucks, tractors and yard trucks.
markets: Customers are miners, farmers and manufacturers; locations beyond the United States are not confirmed.
rationale: B2B industrial automation firm with niche customers; F1 technology tie-in is modest and consumer awareness is low.

name: Bounce
desc: Micromobility company that began with rental scooters and now sells Bounce Infinity electric scooters with swappable batteries and swap stations.
markets: Urban commuters in India buy scooters with a battery-swap network; no international expansion known.
rationale: Indian consumer EV brand focused on urban commuters; F1 offers limited fit for its domestic, price-sensitive market.

name: CalmCar Vision System
desc: Chinese automotive vision company developing deep-learning embedded camera systems for driver assistance, surround view and autonomous driving.
markets: Sells to car makers, apparently in China; overseas customers are not confirmed.
rationale: B2B camera technology supplier with low consumer profile; F1 technology tie-in exists, but fit is weak.

name: Parallel Systems
desc: Developing an autonomous battery-electric freight railcar that carries shipping containers on existing rail lines.
markets: Pre-commercial start-up piloting in the United States, aiming to offer trucking-like flexibility on rail.
rationale: Early-stage freight technology company with no consumer brand; F1 sponsorship is unlikely to suit its stage.

name: Ethernovia
desc: Fabless semiconductor start-up developing automotive Ethernet networking chips that move high-speed data around software-defined vehicles.
markets: Targets automakers and suppliers; commercial shipments and customer locations are not confirmed from the available data.
rationale: Chip start-up whose technology suits automotive showcases, but it has low brand awareness and limited budget.

name: Fisker Automotive
desc: Californian electric car company whose predecessor Fisker Automotive built the Karma plug-in hybrid before bankruptcy.
markets: Built the Karma plug-in hybrid in the United States; the later Fisker Inc. made the Ocean SUV and also failed.
rationale: Defunct brand with no operating business and a history of bankruptcies, so there is no Formula 1 sponsorship case.
changed: Fisker Automotive went bankrupt in 2013; later Fisker Inc. filed in 2024

name: Better Place
desc: Pioneering electric vehicle battery-swapping network founded by Shai Agassi that operated swap stations and cars in Israel and Denmark.
markets: Operated swap stations and electric cars in Israel and Denmark before going bankrupt.
rationale: Company went bankrupt in 2013 and no longer operates, so there is no Formula 1 sponsorship case.

name: Byton
desc: Chinese-German electric vehicle start-up founded in 2017 that designed the M-Byte connected electric SUV, backed by FAW and Tencent.
markets: Planned production in Nanjing for China, with offices in Germany and the United States; production halted.
rationale: Production halted and the start-up is effectively defunct, so there is no realistic Formula 1 sponsorship case.

name: CHJ Automotive
desc: Beijing company described as developing and manufacturing electric vehicles, tagged under automotive and clean technology.
markets: Based in China; models, volumes, funding and ownership are not given.
rationale: Not recognised and details unconfirmed; any F1 fit cannot be judged and appears weak.

name: DS Automobiles
desc: China sales and service operation for DS Automobiles, Stellantis's premium French car marque.
markets: Sells DS cars and provides after-sales service in China; the brand is niche there.
rationale: Niche premium French brand with small Chinese presence; F1 fit is weak because the brand focuses on Formula E.

name: Frontier Car Group
desc: Berlin-based group that built used-car marketplaces such as OLX Autos in Latin America, Asia and Africa.
markets: Operated used-car marketplaces in emerging markets; acquired by OLX Group and integrated into OLX Autos.
rationale: Business was folded into OLX Autos and no longer exists as a brand, so there is no sponsorship case.
changed: Acquired by OLX Group in 2019 and folded into OLX Autos

name: NIUTRON
desc: Beijing company in automotive and clean energy, described as a manufacturer, researcher and developer; products and customers unstated.

name: Teld New Energy
desc: Operates one of China's largest EV charging networks, with hundreds of thousands of charging points, as a subsidiary of TBEA.
markets: Serves EV drivers and fleets across China; no international operations confirmed.
rationale: Large Chinese charging operator without consumer brand marketing; domestic focus makes the F1 fit weak.

name: Titan International
desc: Makes wheels, tires and undercarriage components for agricultural, construction and mining equipment under the Titan and Goodyear Farm Tires brands.
markets: Supplies equipment makers and dealers in North America, Europe and Latin America.
rationale: B2B wheel supplier with farm and construction customers; F1 fit is weak, though hospitality could host OEM partners.

name: Aulton New Energy
desc: Shanghai provider of electric vehicle battery replacement services, per Crunchbase, within the automotive sector.
markets: Likely serves EV owners and fleets in China; scale, ownership and overseas plans are not stated.
rationale: Battery-swap service with limited confirmed details and domestic focus; weak F1 fit.

name: Phylion Battery
desc: Chinese lithium-ion battery maker supplying electric bike, electric vehicle and energy storage customers.
markets: Based in the Suzhou region; customers include vehicle and device manufacturers, with overseas sales not confirmed.
rationale: B2B battery supplier with little consumer brand profile; F1 fit is weak.

name: Tempo Automation
desc: Was a California electronics manufacturing service provider offering fast-turn printed circuit board assembly, later listed through a SPAC merger.
markets: Served US engineering and technology customers before listing on Nasdaq in 2022 and then filing for bankruptcy.
rationale: Company went bankrupt in 2023 and no longer operates, so there is no Formula 1 sponsorship case.
changed: Merged with ACE Convergence in 2022 and filed for bankruptcy in 2023

name: TrueCar
desc: Runs a US online car-buying marketplace that connects shoppers with dealers using price data, earning dealer fees.
markets: Consumers and dealers in the United States; no international operations known.
rationale: US car marketplace with moderate brand awareness; F1 could reach car shoppers, though budget and US focus are limited.

name: Wejo
desc: Was a UK connected vehicle data company that gathered car data for carmakers and mapping firms before listing on Nasdaq.
markets: Collected data from vehicles in several countries before filing for bankruptcy in 2023.
rationale: Company went bankrupt in 2023 and no longer operates, so there is no Formula 1 sponsorship case.

name: Zongmu
desc: Chinese self-driving technology company providing parking assistance sensors, driver-assistance software and autonomous driving systems to car makers.
industry: driver assistance and autonomous driving systems
markets: Sells to automakers and suppliers, apparently in China; overseas customers are not confirmed.
rationale: B2B automotive technology supplier with little consumer profile and mainly Chinese customers, so the Formula 1 fit is weak.

name: LiveWire
desc: Electric motorcycle maker spun out of Harley-Davidson, building the LiveWire S2 Del Mar and One electric motorcycles.
markets: Sells motorcycles through dealers in North America and Europe; majority held by Harley-Davidson.
rationale: Premium electric motorcycle brand with two-region reach; F1 could show electrification credentials, though sales scale is small.

name: Tritium
desc: Australian-founded maker of DC fast chargers for electric vehicles, whose assets were bought by India's Exicom in 2024.
markets: Founded in Brisbane in 2001; sold chargers in Australia, Europe and North America before collapsing.
rationale: Charging hardware brand now owned by Exicom; F1 could showcase charging technology, though budget is limited.
changed: Assets acquired by Exicom in 2024 after administration

name: TrustMotion
desc: Austrian automotive software and hardware company providing safety and sensing solutions for autonomous driving, according to Crunchbase.
markets: Based in Austria; customers would be car makers and suppliers, but sales and overseas activity are not confirmed.
rationale: B2B technology start-up with low awareness and unconfirmed scale; weak F1 fit.

name: Battle Motors
desc: Makes vocational and electric trucks, such as refuse and utility trucks, for municipal and waste fleets.
markets: Customers are municipal and waste fleets in the United States.
rationale: B2B truck maker with low awareness and a domestic fleet audience; weak F1 fit.

name: Innovusion
desc: Makes lidar sensors for autonomous vehicles, founded in Silicon Valley with large China operations, supplying carmakers including NIO.
markets: Operates in the United States and China; the business was merged into Seyond.
rationale: B2B sensor supplier now part of Seyond; F1 technology tie-in is modest and consumer awareness is low.

name: Superpedestrian
desc: Made Link electric scooters with robotic safety features for city rental programmes before shutting down in 2023.
markets: Operated rental scooters in US and European cities before closing in December 2023.
rationale: Company shut down in December 2023 and no longer operates, so there is no Formula 1 sponsorship case.

name: Accelerated Brands
